brief:
RESULT STATUS: NOT PUBLIC

No double-blind ADEPT-2 result has been released. BMS's November 2026 CTAD presentation covered only open-label data from ADEPT-1 and ADEPT-3, and the double-blind treatment periods in all ADEPT studies remain blinded. ([BMS release](https://news.bms.com/news/details/2026/Bristol-Myers-Squibb-Presents-First-Clinical-Data-from-Two-Phase-3-Studies-in-the-ADEPT-Program-Evaluating-KarXT-for-Psychosis-Associated-with-Alzheimers-Disease/default.aspx)). The open-label numbers (NPI-C H+D fell by 12.0 points from 14.4 (n=266) in the ADEPT-1 lead-in) are uncontrolled and should not be read as efficacy evidence.

**Earlier trials in this disease**
- Only prior controlled data: Bodick 1997, a 6-month xanomeline monotherapy trial in 343 patients. The cognitive completer analysis was significant at p=0.045 for the top dose, and dose-dependent reductions in vocal outbursts, suspiciousness, delusions, agitation, and hallucinations were reported, though not as a primary endpoint ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9339268/)). At the highest dose, xanomeline therapy resulted in treatment discontinuation in more than half of participants ([Psychiatrist.com](https://www.psychiatrist.com/news/exploring-the-link-between-schizophrenia-and-alzheimers/)).
- No prior KarXT double-blind AD-psychosis efficacy data found.

**Same disease, other mechanisms**
- Pimavanserin: a phase 2 AD-psychosis trial showed improved psychosis at week 6, which was the prespecified timepoint (p=0·045), and a later phase 3 in long-term care showed no benefit over placebo at 12 weeks ([Lancet Neurology](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/laneur/article/PIIS1474-4422(21)00466-X/fulltext); [Carlat](https://www.thecarlatreport.com/articles/4163-can-pimavanserin-treat-psychosis-in-patients-with-dementia)).
- Placebo-controlled antipsychotic trials in dementia psychosis are mixed: clozapine (n = 2) and pimavanserin (n = 2) showed benefit, with no firm benefits observed for quetiapine (n = 4) or olanzapine (n = 3) ([ResearchGate review](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380273620_Pimavanserin_for_Psychosis_in_Parkinson's_Disease_Dementia_Subgroup_Analysis_of_the_HARMONY_Trial)).

**Same drug, other disease**
- Schizophrenia: the prespecified primary efficacy endpoint was met in all three EMERGENT trials, with a pooled PANSS difference of −9.9; 95% confidence interval, –12.4, –7.3; p < 0.0001 ([Schizophrenia journal](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41537-024-00525-6)).
- An add-on schizophrenia trial failed: a 400-person schizophrenia study found it not significantly better than a placebo as an add-on treatment ([BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/bristol-myers-cobenfy-alzheimers-psychosis-adept-2-trial-update-timeline/806917/)).

**Base rate and comparator**
- I found no systematic success-rate tally for AD-psychosis trials. The comparator is placebo, and I found no placebo-response data for this trial.

**Sponsor statements, powering, and design changes**
- Dec 2025: BMS identified "irregularities" in the way the study was conducted at a "small number" of sites, excluded those sites' data from the primary analysis, and, after an independent interim review, a data monitoring committee recommended the trial keep going and enroll more participants ([Yahoo/BioPharma Dive](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/finding-irregularities-bristol-myers-extend-120200832.html)).
- July 2026: the CEO attributed the delay to slower enrollment in the Adept-2 and Adept-4 studies and slower relapse event accrual in Adept-1. The CMO said this scrutiny in preserving quality and increasing quality impacted the enrollment pace ([Q2 call transcript](https://www.roic.ai/quote/BMY:LN/transcripts/2026-year/2-quarter)). Readouts now begin in early 2027 and be "spread across the year".
- Design drift: the 2023 design abstract described 12 weeks of double-blind treatment and approximately 360 subjects. The record now lists 14 weeks and 500 estimated enrollment. Another source gives a 400-patient target ([Alzforum](https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/karxt)).
- Analyst skepticism: one analyst said none of this suggests an overwhelmingly positive result ([BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/bristol-myers-cobenfy-alzheimers-psychosis-adept-2-trial-update-timeline/806917/)).
- Sponsor confidence: BMS said there has been no change in any way in our confidence in both the underlying science and the study designs.
rationale: KarXT's muscarinic mechanism is validated in schizophrenia and xanomeline showed signals against psychotic symptoms in AD, but AD-psychosis trials have a high failure rate, driven by strong placebo response, as with pimavanserin's phase 3 and the mixed antipsychotic data. The DMC's interim recommendation to enlarge enrollment from about 360 to 500 suggests an observed effect smaller than planned (a promising-zone style increase), and the site irregularities and add-on schizophrenia failure add uncertainty. The sample increase does improve power, and anticholinergic tolerability is managed by trospium, so I land near a coin flip.

brief:
**RESULT STATUS: NOT PUBLIC**

I found no topline release, publication, or conference presentation of Beamion LUNG-2's primary PFS result. Boehringer's mid-2026 materials still call the study an ongoing Phase III controlled study ([BI ASCO 2026 release, May 2026](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/21/3299786/0/en/Boehringer-Ingelheim-s-oncology-portfolio-shows-strong-promise-across-multiple-cancers-at-ASCO-2026.html)).

**Enrollment and sponsor statements**
- Publications planned about 270 patients randomized 1:1 ([ASCO TPS abstract](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.TPS8654)). The record shows 428 actual enrolled. I found no explanation for the gap.
- At a 2026 meeting, the investigator Heymach said "Target enrollment has been reached" ([OncLive](https://www.onclive.com/view/frontline-zongertinib-shows-systemic-and-intracranial-activity-in-advanced-her2-mutant-nsclc)).
- I found no statements on powering, interim analyses, design changes, or delays.

**Earlier zongertinib data (same drug, same disease)**
- Phase Ib LUNG-1 cohort 2 (n=74, treatment-naïve, single-arm, ORR primary): confirmed ORR 76% (95% CI 65–84), median DoR 15.2 months, and median PFS 14.4 months ([NEJM/BI release](https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com/us/human-health/cancer/lung-cancer/nejm-publishes-results-patients-her2-mutant-nsclc); [CancerNetwork](https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/zongertinib-yields-enduring-activity-in-frontline-her2-nsclc-trial)). No comparator, p-value, or randomization.
- FDA accelerated approval in February 2026 rested on that ORR ([BI FDA release](https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com/us/human-health/cancer/lung-cancer/fda-approves-targeted-therapy-her2-mutant-advanced-nsclc)).

**Same mechanism, other drugs**
- Sevabertinib (reversible HER2 TKI), SOHO-01 cohort F, n=69 treatment-naïve: ORR 75% (95% CI 64–85), single-arm, no PFS reported ([Lung Summit](https://lungsummit.org/articles/sevabertinib-approved-in-the-us-for-untreated-her2-mutant-nsclc/)). Its phase 3 confirmatory trial, SOHO-02 (n=444), is versus standard of care ([Lung Summit](https://lungsummit.org/articles/sevabertinib-approved-in-the-us-for-untreated-her2-mutant-nsclc/)).
- Trastuzumab deruxtecan (HER2 ADC, not a TKI) in DESTINY-Lung04, a randomized phase 3 with the same control arm (n=454): median PFS 14.3 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.50–0.79) ([AstraZeneca](https://www.astrazeneca.com/media-centre/press-releases/2026/enhertu-in-DESTINY-Lung04-Phase-iii-trial.html); [Dana-Farber](https://www.dana-farber.org/newsroom/news-releases/2026/phase-3-destiny-lung04-trial-shows-first-line-trastuzumab-deruxtecan-improves-progression-free-survival-in-her2-mutant-nsclc)). OS was immature and HR 1.15, with imbalanced later therapy ([Pharmacy/AllSci](https://allsci.com/news/clinical-trials/her2-mutant-lung-cancer-enhertu-cuts-progression/)). This is the closest evidence that the control arm can be beaten on PFS in this population.

**Comparator and PFS base rates**
- KEYNOTE-189, which did not select for HER2, reported median PFS 8.8 months ([EMJ review](https://www.emjreviews.com/oncology/symposium/updates-in-first-line-treatment-of-advanced-her2-erbb2-mutant-non-small-cell-lung-cancer-insights-from-the-european-society-for-medical-oncology-esmo-congress-2025-s33525/)).
- A review of small HER2-mutant cohorts reported first-line chemotherapy ORR of 43.5% and median PFS of about 6 months ([PMC review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12125733)). These are older, pooled, and small.
- I did not find a systematic tally of how often first-line HER2-mutant phase 3 trials have met PFS endpoints.

**Other diseases**
- Zongertinib in HER2-positive metastatic colorectal cancer: ORR 42% (n=8 of 20 pooled) ([BI ASCO 2026](https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com/human-health/cancer/oncology-portfolio-across-multiple-cancers-asco-2026)). Breast and gastric data are early.
rationale: Zongertinib showed a 76% confirmed ORR and 14.4-month median PFS in treatment-naïve HER2-mutant NSCLC, and DESTINY-Lung04 has already shown that the same pembrolizumab-platinum-pemetrexed control can be beaten on PFS in this population (HR 0.63, control median about 8.3 months). Targeted TKIs against chemo-IO in oncogene-driven NSCLC usually win on PFS. Enrollment grew to 428 from the planned ~270, which adds power even if the effect is moderate. The main risks are a durable immunotherapy tail in the control arm and possible discordance between local and central HER2 testing, but a significant PFS benefit looks likely.
